system_description.narrative_title: Iran war: US actions, regional spillover, and mediation efforts
system_description.narrative_summary: The dominant narrative describes an active US–Iran conflict shaped by US strikes and Iranian reprisals, widening regional involvement, and intensive mediation efforts (notably by Qatar) to avert broader escalation. As an open system, military actions, diplomatic channels, domestic political feedback (US midterms and Trump-era calculations), and energy-market shocks enter and exit the system, creating reinforcing escalation loops and pressure for negotiated outcomes. Concrete actors (the US administration, Iran, Gulf states, Houthi forces, Russia, Qatar) interact through systemic variables — escalation risk, mediation efficacy, economic chokepoints, and domestic political costs — producing uncertain cascade effects across the region and global markets.
system_description.scope: The conflict system bounded here includes US–Iran military interactions and retaliations; regional proxy and state responses (Houthis, Saudi Arabia, UAE, Bahrain, Syria, Russia); mediation and diplomatic channels (Qatar, UN, backchannels); economic levers (naval blockades, sanctions, oil and LNG flows); domestic political feedback in the US and regional states; and immediate humanitarian and escalation consequences.
system_description.super_system: Global geopolitical and security order, including international diplomatic institutions and global energy markets
adjacent_subsystems: Global energy markets (oil & LNG prices and supply chains)
US domestic politics and electoral incentives
Gulf states' security and inter-state diplomacy

variables.name: Escalation pressure
variables.description: The aggregate latent tendency for violent escalation measured by frequency, intensity, and proximity of hostile actions and retaliations.

variables.name: Kinetic operations rate
variables.description: The tempo at which conventional and strike military operations are initiated and executed across the theatre.

variables.name: Proxy forces activity
variables.description: The operational activity level of irregular and proxy actors, including attacks, mobilizations, and cross-border actions.

variables.name: Diplomatic engagement intensity
variables.description: The volume and frequency of formal and informal diplomatic contacts, negotiations, and backchannel communications.

variables.name: Mediation effectiveness
variables.description: The capacity of third-party facilitation to reduce tensions and produce credible, implementable de‑escalation outcomes.

variables.name: Economic chokepoint vulnerability
variables.description: The degree to which critical trade routes and transit nodes are exposed to interdiction, disruption, or denial.

variables.name: Energy price volatility
variables.description: The variability of global energy commodity prices driven by disruptions, market sentiment, and supply/demand shifts.

variables.name: Sanctions pressure level
variables.description: The aggregate intensity and scope of economic restrictive measures affecting trade, finance, and access to markets.

variables.name: Domestic political costs
variables.description: The political liability or benefit experienced by governing actors from ongoing conflict, reflected in approval, mobilization, and electoral risk.

variables.name: Public sentiment polarization
variables.description: The degree of societal division over the conflict measured by intensity and dispersion of opposing public views.

variables.name: Humanitarian need level
variables.description: The scale of urgent civilian needs for shelter, food, medical care, and displacement support arising from hostilities.

variables.name: Military logistics resilience
variables.description: The robustness of supply, sustainment, and mobility chains supporting military operations under stress or interdiction.

variables.name: Arms and ammunition flow
variables.description: The rate and volume of weapons, munitions, and related materiel moving into and within the conflict system.

variables.name: Alliance cohesion strength
variables.description: The stability and alignment of cooperative security relationships manifested in coordinated policy, public statements, and joint actions.

variables.name: Negotiation momentum
variables.description: The rate of forward movement in talks measured by proposal exchanges, concessions, and scheduling of follow‑up steps.

variables.name: Regional economic disruption
variables.description: The extent of trade, investment, and fiscal disturbances across the region caused by conflict-related shocks and precautionary measures.

catalysts.title: Qatar-led mediation advances
catalysts.description: Qatar continues shuttle diplomacy between Washington and Tehran, carrying Iranian proposals and pressing for a deal to halt fighting.
catalysts.rationale: Qatar emir call; Qatar says mediation continues; Iran sent nuclear proposal via Qatar; mediators push for deal. [2026-11-06][2026-11-07]

catalysts.title: US expands restrictions on Iranian commerce
catalysts.description: US plans to widen maritime and land measures to restrict Iranian trade flows, including expanded naval interdiction and land-commerce limits.
catalysts.rationale: 'Expanding on naval blockade, US military looks to restrict Iranian land commerce' signals imminent broader interdiction. [2026-11-07]

catalysts.title: Risk of additional limited US strikes
catalysts.description: Elevated chance of further 'minor' US strikes against Iranian targets or related assets in response to provocations or adviser pressure.
catalysts.rationale: Trump says US carried out 'minor strikes'; advisers press for decisions; risk of escalation remains high. [2026-11-07][2026-11-07]

catalysts.title: Escalation cycle in Yemen and Red Sea
catalysts.description: Houthi attacks and Saudi responses (with wider regional involvement) will likely continue, driving proxy exchanges and maritime risk.
catalysts.rationale: Houthi-run health ministry reports deadly strikes; Saudi weighs responses; Syria assisting Saudi amid Houthi attacks. [2026-11-08][2026-11-06][2026-11-07]

catalysts.title: Russian arms transfers to Iran deepen
catalysts.description: Ongoing Russian deliveries (missile launchers, etc.) increase Tehran's strike capability and resupply timeline.
catalysts.rationale: Report: 'Russia deepened Iran support with missile launcher deal' increases Iranian capabilities and regional tensions. [2026-11-06]

catalysts.title: Humanitarian needs spike among displaced
catalysts.description: Weather, overcrowding, and aid shortfalls worsen conditions for displaced civilians, creating urgent relief gaps.
catalysts.rationale: Heavy rain floods tents housing displaced people; aid shortages hamper response. [2026-11-07]

catalysts.title: Energy market volatility from conflict fears
catalysts.description: Markets react to attack and strike risks, driving short-term crude and LNG price swings tied to regional disruptions.
catalysts.rationale: Crude gains on worries about renewed US attacks; Qatar LNG developments affect market sensitivity. [2026-11-07][2026-11-06]

catalysts.title: US political recalibration after midterms
catalysts.description: Post-midterm U.S. political dynamics will shape decisions on the Iran war, constraining or accelerating military and diplomatic moves.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines ask 'What's Next for Iran Peace Talks After the Midterms' and link war to electoral outcomes. [2026-11-06][2026-11-06]
